headline: The Lean and Mathlib communities certify the AI-assisted Riemann proof, Nvidia ends its worst week since 2008, NATO vows to defend every inch of Poland, two more tankers are hit off Oman, and toxic liquor kills at least 11 in Manipur
standfirst: In tech, a joint Lean and Mathlib statement accepts Levent Alpöge's 17-million-line Lean proof, Nvidia loses nearly $900 billion in a week, and the FBI investigates an apparent hack of its national crime database. On /geo/, COP31 puts a final text to a Sunday vote and Mexico captures cartel boss El Chapo Isidro. On /krieg/, Rutte speaks in Warsaw before Monday's NATO council on the missiles in Poland, tankers are hit near Khasab, and Iran strikes an industrial site in Bahrain. In India, at least 11 die from toxic liquor in Manipur and Pant's 128 puts India more than 300 ahead in Wellington. On /cinema/, Sunrise on the Reaping heads for a $120 million-plus opening and Ramayana Part 1 passes Rs 900 crore net in India.
notes: Phoenix run for 22 November, started by hand at 07:06 IST and assembled by Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5); five research agents of the same model wrote the boards. No browser was connected: the X feed and the X accounts @aravind and @keshavbedi were not read (no browser connected), and Moctale was not fetched (bot check). Web searches for trending tech news stood in for the X feed. Ground News: the World page returned only its title; the Daily Briefing page gave source counts. The Reddit fetch had produced no output when the Cinema board was written, so no Cinema card has a Reddit rank. On the Riemann card: the 21 November edition called Alpöge's claim a proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis; the Lean community statement certifies that the proved theorem matches Mathlib's statement of the Riemann Hypothesis. At assembly, pronouns for the Studio Display blogger were removed (not stated in the source).

Tech: the X feed was not reachable this run (no browser), so one extended WebSearch ('trending tech news today 22 November 2026') stood in for it, plus searches on the Nvidia SEC probe and Anthropic stock, the FBI NCIC hack, Brazil's tax calculator and reaction to the Lean verification. Read the Hacker News front page (day max 2391 pts) and these primary pages: Lean community blog, Andrew Sutherland's MIT verification page, LookAtMyQuant repo, Mozilla blog, tymscar blog, GnuPG advisory, the machine-code blog, Zero C#, gopgext, pwn.ai Upload2Shell, Nvidia blog, TechCrunch and CNBC Technology front pages, TechCrunch on the FBI hack, CNBC on Anthropic and on Jensen Huang, Yahoo Finance on Nvidia, AP (via KSAT) on the FBI hack, Scientific American, Tecnoblog. The gov.br press release for Brazil returned 404, so that card uses Tecnoblog. Nature redirected to a login page and was not used. GRH: the Masullo post (HN 2391) is pure mathematics with no AI angle and appears only as context inside the Lean card. Left out: pancreatic cancer pill, lead azide, unemployment Ask HN, mind/body essay, MTG, rainforest, Corded Ware (not tech, owner rule); Signal's mobile screenshot limit (TechCrunch 21 Nov), because it is part of the 20 November announcement carried yesterday; Nvidia RTX Spark mini PCs (launched 18 November, outside the window); lower-heat HN items (Rust GUIs, PcapAnalyzer, Pandex, GTA VI profiling claim). Arithmetic: none of our own. Unverified cards: the Inkling quant numbers (author's own) and the Studio Display finding (one user's blog).

Geopolitics: read the Ground News home page and Daily Briefing (21-22 Nov edition, 8 stories with source counts and bias splits). The Ground News World page (ground.news/interest/world) returned empty, only a page title. WebSearch (extended) for top world news 22 Nov, Ground News international stories, COP31 outcome, Eisenkot/Likud, US-China trade, elections, disasters, plus follow-ups. Left out as war-related: Iran 'dirty bomb' warning, Hormuz tanker incidents, Qeshm Island blasts, Houthi missiles at Jazan, Denmark expelling Russia's defence attache over the plot to kill Ukrainian-American rapper Kyivstoner (Russian hybrid attack, belongs with the Ukraine war), NATO pledge to Poland. Left out as outside the 20-22 Nov window: ICJ ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya (19 Nov), Takaichi's cool reception in China (18-19 Nov), Ninth Circuit stay on Venezuelan TPS (order dated 18 Nov), US Southwest floods (early Nov). Not carried forward because nothing new: Shenzhen US-China trade aftermath (only a Reuters analysis on 21 Nov, no new talks), Bukele third term, UAE-Somalia, Canada tariffs, Supreme Court climate grants, American Samoa leases (only new detail: $6 million in high bids). No national election or referendum found for 20-22 Nov. COP31 approval was still pending when searched (plenary set for 06:00 GMT on 22 Nov); the outcome is not confirmed. Unverified card: Peru earthquake (Anadolu only).

Krieg: read Al Jazeera (Hormuz tankers, Poland explainer, Houthi missiles), the CBS News Iran live page, France 24 (Ukraine, Rutte in Warsaw), NBC News (Gaza truck strike), straits.live 22 Nov brief, plus WebSearch (extended) for every live war. Ground News World page returned only its title, so no Ground News source counts are used in heat lines; globalsecurity.org, Benzinga, Sudan Tribune, Mizzima and US News were blocked (403) or timed out. Left out for lack of news dated 20-22 Nov: DRC and M23 (latest dated ~9 Nov), Myanmar (only resistance-aligned notes, no verifiable dated strike), the Sahel (latest 13 Nov), Pakistan-Afghanistan (latest raids 19 Nov), Kashmir (latest encounter 18 Nov), Ethiopia-Eritrea (latest ACLED items to 18 Nov). Oil prices folded into the Hormuz card. Unverified cards: bahrain-iran-strike-industrial-site-fire (Iranian claims on US bases rest on the IRGC), houthis-fire-three-missiles-riyadh (casualty claims are one-sided), sudan-rsf-accused-killing-civilians-abu-qalb (one rights monitor, article not opened).

India: read the Ground News India page (Manipur liquor deaths, Adani Defence missile test and the Owaisi guard-of-honour mix-up were its top stories; Quad 'economic coercion' was flagged as a Blindspot with only 7% Left coverage but dates from the 17 November Manila summit, so it was left out as too old) and extended web searches on the day's headlines, markets, the Nepal visit, Ladakh polls, the Wellington Test, the Nitish Setu, Tata Sons, RBI, Delhi air and state politics. The X accounts @aravind and @keshavbedi could not be read (no browser connected). Left out: war and Kashmir items (Krieg board), film news (Cinema board), the reported death of Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Vadkute (only Marathi outlets, place of death differs between them), and the Nagpur renaming demand (small). Carried forward with new developments: Nepal visit (arrival day, agenda), Wellington Test (day four), markets (weekly totals), Modi's Bihar tour (opposition row), Ladakh polls (turnout), Tata Sons (pre-board moves). Unverified: Tata Trusts pre-board meeting card (one secondary source). Manipur death toll differs: 11 per the chief minister via Reuters/AP, 16 per Oneindia.

Cinema: read WebSearch (extended) for Bollywood and Hollywood news of 20-22 November, the Sunrise on the Reaping weekend, and Sacnilk, Koimoi, Bollywood Hungama and ETV Bharat for Ramayana day 17 and O.M day 2. Read primary pages: Sacnilk day pages for Ramayana and O.M, TheWrap's Saturday box office report, the Bollywood Hungama news list and its Salman Khan article, Daijiworld on the IFFI opening. The Hollywood Reporter redirected to its paid bot gateway (tollbit), so it was not followed; THR, Deadline and Variety facts come from search summaries and outlets quoting them. Moctale was not tried (bot check, no browser this run). Reddit: the top-today RSS file was still empty when read once at the end, so no Reddit heat is in any score; scores rest on outlet breadth and velocity only. Sunday actuals for the US weekend were not out at writing time, so the $120 million is a Saturday projection. O.M day 2 figures differ by tracker (Sacnilk Rs 15.40 crore, ETV Bharat Rs 10.76 crore); Sacnilk is used and the gap is stated. Left out: Robert Pattinson as James Bond (announced 16 November, outside the window), Tom Cruise's Digger losses (October), Haiwaan (released September), the Gemma Chan Bond comment and small items such as the D'YAVOL X and Golden Goose collection. No blind-item gossip carried. The Saif Ali Khan threat card is marked unverified on the threat details, which come from police statements relayed by the press and are still under forensic check.

sections.title: Tech
sections.blurb: Lean and Mathlib communities certify Alpöge's AI-assisted Riemann Hypothesis proof, Nvidia ends its worst week since 2008, the FBI investigates an apparent hack of its national crime database, and Anthropic closes its debut week at $88.91.

stories.title: The Lean and Mathlib communities say they have full confidence in Levent Alpöge's AI-assisted Lean proof of the Riemann Hypothesis.
stories.summary: A joint statement on 21 November says several independent checkers accepted the 17-million-line proof and that the proved theorem matches Mathlib's statement of the Riemann Hypothesis. MIT's Andrew Sutherland published verification files showing the build compiles with zero errors and uses only the standard axioms.
stories.heat: HN 828 pts / 674 comments (Lean blog) plus 93 pts / 36 comments (MIT verification files) · Lean FRO, Mathlib Initiative, Scientific American, TechCrunch · velocity: high, statement posted 21 Nov
stories.about: Levent Alpöge is a number theorist who works at Anthropic and says he found the proof with Claude. Lean is a proof assistant that checks each step of a formal proof; Mathlib is its shared mathematics library.
detail: What is new since yesterday: the proof has moved from 'it compiles' to a formal community certification. In a joint statement dated 21 November and endorsed by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative, the Lean and Mathlib communities say the library of about 17 million lines depends only on Mathlib, that 'dozens of people have reported correct compilation', and that the statement proved is Mathlib's own RiemannHypothesis, 'carefully vetted by experts in Lean and number theory'.

The statement says the exported proof was checked by Lean's kernel and by the independent checkers con-leche and con-ron, among others, and that two tools (comparator and con-leche --compare) confirmed the proved theorem matches Mathlib's statement. The checks ran on an inert export of the proof, out of reach of any malicious code in the sources. It says all four criteria set out in a Xena blog post on 12 November are met.

Andrew Sutherland's MIT page, last updated 21 November at 12:55 UTC, lists the details: all 175,187 modules compile under Lean and Mathlib v4.33.1 with zero errors; the five main theorems use only the standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound); the independent kernel nanoda accepts the export in about 28 minutes on 80 threads and con-leche in about 3 minutes on 64 threads. Some runs were still going, including the Lean default and paranoid kernels and an end-to-end lake comparator run, which needs about 100 GB of RAM.

Scope: Sutherland's page says the checked theorems cover the Riemann Hypothesis and Dirichlet L-functions, including GRH for primitive characters, but that 'Dedekind zeta functions, Hecke L-functions and automorphic L-functions in general are not among the statements that were checked'. It also notes the result 'relies on those kernels and on Mathlib's definitions being what they are intended to be'.

Scientific American updated its report on 21 November. It quotes Sutherland saying the chance anything is 'fishy here is approximately zero', and Kevin Buzzard of Imperial College London on why the statement check matters. Machine certification is not human understanding: Alpöge has still released no full human-readable paper.

Context: a separate, fully human proposed proof of GRH by Stanford postdoc Alessandro Masullo, posted by Ravi Vakil on 20 November, is the day's top Hacker News item (2391 pts). It has no AI angle and no Lean version.

stories.title: Nvidia lost nearly $900 billion in market value this week, its worst week since October 2008, as investigations into the company widen.
stories.summary: Nvidia's 14% fall on 20 November capped a seven-week losing streak, the longest since 2008, CNBC reports. California's attorney general has subpoenaed the company over chips reaching China, and Trump says he would like Jensen Huang to get 'a second chance'.
stories.heat: No HN thread today · CNBC, Yahoo Finance, Reuters, TechCrunch, Bloomberg · velocity: high, weekend follow-ups 21 Nov
detail: What is new since yesterday's card: the week's totals and the wider set of probes. Yahoo Finance reported on 21 November that Nvidia lost about $490 billion in market value on Friday and nearly $900 billion over the week, its worst week since October 2008. The previous week's $573 billion loss had been the biggest one-week drop for any company on record, and Nvidia has lost about $2.7 trillion since its 6 October record. CNBC puts the weekly fall at 23% and the losing streak at seven weeks, the longest since 2008.

Investigations: Reuters reports that the SEC is examining potential accounting issues, and the Wall Street Journal says the probe includes whether disclosures misled investors. California Attorney General Rob Bonta subpoenaed Nvidia on Thursday 19 November over whether its advanced chips reached China and whether it misled investors: 'Companies cannot mislead their investors.' Nvidia has delayed its 10-Q filing to 'the coming weeks', and its earnings release mentions an investigation by an independent board committee.

Politics: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said answers are needed 'in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel' after Jensen Huang's exit as chief executive. Trump said on Friday he 'would love to see Jensen be given a second chance'. CNBC reports Huang will testify in public before the Senate banking committee, with no date set yet, and has agreed to a closed-door interview with three House committees on 1 December.

sources.name: CNBC: Nvidia longest losing streak since 2008
CNBC: Huang to testify before Senate banking panel

stories.title: The FBI is investigating an apparent hack of the National Crime Information Center, the database police across the US use for warrants and records.
stories.summary: CNN first reported the intrusion and AP confirmed it through a person familiar with the matter. The scope is not clear, and Trump said on 21 November: 'it's not good.'
stories.heat: No HN thread · CNN, AP, ABC News, Al Jazeera, Forbes, TechCrunch, CNBC, BleepingComputer · velocity: high, reported 20-21 Nov
detail: AP reported on 21 November that the FBI is investigating an apparent hack of the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), a database that local, state and federal agencies use for records on fugitives, missing persons, criminal history and stolen property. CNN reported the incident first on 20 November. The FBI declined to comment on Saturday, and AP says the scope of the problem was not immediately clear.

A former FBI official told CNN the concerns are whether hackers reached sensitive information and whether they could tamper with records officers rely on, TechCrunch reports. Trump told Fox News: 'We just heard about it and I will say that it's not good,' and later suggested the breach could have a 'positive spin'. AP lists earlier FBI incidents this year: 'suspicious activities' on an internal surveillance system disclosed in March, and the ShinyHunters group's claim in September to have taken data on FBI employees and applicants. BleepingComputer says there is no sign the NCIC incident is linked to ShinyHunters.

stories.title: Anthropic shares ended their first trading week at $88.91, as the Nasdaq had its worst week since early 2020.
stories.summary: CNBC reports Anthropic closed Friday at $88.91, after opening at $111.50 on Thursday, for a fully diluted value of $1.6 trillion. The Nasdaq fell 10% over five trading days.
stories.heat: No HN thread today · CNBC, CoinDesk, Yahoo Finance · velocity: moderate, weekend wrap 21 Nov
detail: What is new since yesterday's card: CNBC's 21 November wrap gives the Friday closing price, $88.91, against a Thursday opening of $111.50, and a fully diluted market value of $1.6 trillion at week's end, down from $1.8 trillion after the first day. The IPO raised $93.5 billion, plus $26 billion from tech companies that bought at the offer price.

CNBC says the Nasdaq fell 10% over the past five trading days, its worst week since the start of Covid in 2020, and Nvidia dropped 23%. Analysts are debating whether Anthropic will trade with AI hardware stocks or on its own as an AI developer. CoinDesk tied Bitcoin's fall to fresh lows below $59,000 to the same AI sell-off.

stories.title: A developer has squeezed Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini into 5.4 GB of memory, and a 12.8 GB build matches the original on the tests run.
stories.summary: The open-source LookAtMyQuant project published four compressed builds of the open-weights model. The smallest fits in 5.4 GB but loses ground on coding tests, the author's own numbers show.
stories.heat: HN 354 pts / 91 comments (quant repo, 21 Nov) after 1385 pts for the launch on 20 Nov · GitHub · velocity: moderate
stories.about: Inkling 2 Mini is an open-weights mixture-of-experts model that Thinking Machines Lab released on 20 November. LookAtMyQuant is an MIT-licensed quantization tool by the GitHub user ShinMegamiBoson.
detail: What is new since yesterday's launch card: early uptake by the local-model community. The LookAtMyQuant repo lists four builds made from the model's 18.89 GB of text weights. The 12.8 GB build scores the same as the BF16 original on the tests run (96.5% on a 200-problem GSM8K subset and 92.7% on HumanEval). The 8.9 GB build scores 96.0% and 90.9%.

The 5.4 GB build drops to 88.0% on GSM8K and 70.7% on HumanEval. The author reports 112.7 tokens per second decode for the 12.8 GB build on an Apple M5 Max. All figures are the author's own and use test subsets.

stories.title: Brazil's federal tax authority, the Receita Federal, has published the code of its tax reform calculator on GitHub under the MIT licence.
stories.summary: It is the first time the Receita Federal has released software in public repositories. The three projects calculate the new CBS, IBS and Selective Tax and can be built into business software.
stories.heat: HN 750 pts / 241 comments · Tecnoblog, IT Forum, Diolinux · velocity: moderate, announced 16 Nov, trending on HN 21-22 Nov
detail: Tecnoblog reports that the Receita Federal announced the release on 16 November, authorised by Portaria Cotec nº 342 of 12 November. There are three repositories: the calculator for the regular regime (CBS, IBS and the Imposto Seletivo, plus checks of official tax tables and fiscal document data), a Simples Nacional calculator, and a service that generates PDF documents for NFS-e electronic service invoices.

The code was built with the state IT company Serpro and is MIT-licensed, so it can be used in commercial software. Tecnoblog notes the projects are components for companies' systems, not replacements for them. The calculator had been downloadable since 2025; the GitHub release is the new part.

stories.title: Mozilla says Apple's conditions still keep any browser without WebKit off the iPhone, nearly three years after the EU forced Apple to open up.
stories.summary: In a blog post on 20 November, Mozilla says no developer has launched a non-WebKit browser on iOS under Apple's EU or Japan rules. It says its efforts to improve Apple's conditions have 'largely failed'.
stories.heat: HN 486 pts / 269 comments · Mozilla blog · velocity: moderate, posted 20 Nov
detail: Mozilla says Apple's EU conditions under the Digital Markets Act make it 'as painful as possible' to ship an alternative engine such as Gecko. They would require a separate second Firefox app, with users moving bookmarks, passwords and history by hand. Japan's similar rules, in force for almost a year, came with very similar conditions, and one condition bars Mozilla from disclosing non-public information about the project.

Mozilla says millions of people in the EU have picked Firefox as their default browser and that its daily use on iOS has doubled. It calls Gecko the last major browser engine not built by a big tech company and says it will keep pushing for a 'level playing field'.

stories.title: A blogger found that an Ethernet adapter plugged into an Apple Studio Display XDR cut the blogger's download speed from 2.3 Gbps to about 600 Mbps.
stories.summary: The cause was an adapter chip that sends only four packets per burst, combined with delay added by the monitor's USB hub. An adapter with a newer Realtek chip fixed it.
stories.heat: HN 484 pts / 232 comments · tymscar blog · velocity: moderate, post dated 15 Nov, on HN 21 Nov
detail: On a 2.5 Gbps line, the writer measured about 600 Mbps down through a UGREEN adapter on the 2026 Studio Display XDR, against 2.3 Gbps with the adapter plugged straight into the Mac. The adapter's Realtek RTL8156B chip waited for the Mac after every four packets, the hub's delay made each wait longer, and the dropped frames made the router back off.

Turning on flow control on the router raised downloads to about 2 Gbps. Swapping to an adapter with the RTL8157 chip, which sends eight packets per burst, removed the dropped frames at every tested rate up to 2.4 Gbps.

stories.title: GnuPG warns of a critical double-free bug in its GPGME library, triggered by an OpenPGP key with a very long user ID.
stories.summary: All GPGME versions before 2.3.0 are affected, and the fix is GPGME 2.3.1, released on 19 November. GnuPG says data theft is possible and remote code execution cannot be ruled out.
stories.heat: HN 232 pts / 93 comments · GnuPG announce list · velocity: moderate, disclosed 20 Nov
detail: The advisory (CVE-2026-129975) says a crafted key can trigger the bug when an application processes it, for example while handling signed data. Affected software includes Gpg4win, GnuPG Desktop, most mail clients, many XMPP clients, Samba and Flatpak, and statically linked programs must be rebuilt. Johan Carlsson found the bug; GnuPG disclosed it on 20 November, five days early, because GitLab had to ship its own update sooner.

stories.title: Two researchers show that an AI model can read, patch and write working Linux executables directly from hex dumps, with no compiler or disassembler.
stories.summary: George Xenos and Sotiris Giannopoulos report that GPT-6.1 Sol explained four binaries, patched three to pass hidden tests and wrote three new programs from a spec. The authors call the results early, from small programs and single runs.
stories.heat: HN 192 pts / 125 comments · personal research blog · velocity: low to moderate, posted 18 Nov
detail: Sol also found a bug in FreeBSD's ministat and analysed a 4,608-byte malware sample, recovering its server address and 13 API hashes, which a public sandbox report matched. The open-weights DeepSeek V4.1 Flash reached the same malware verdict but named only 9 of the 13 APIs and used about 17 times as many reasoning tokens. Hex costs about 2.4 tokens per byte, so the largest test, 67 KB, used about 163,000 tokens.

stories.title: Zero C# is a new fork of the bflat compiler that turns C# into small native programs with no .NET runtime and no garbage collector.
stories.summary: Memory comes from arenas that are freed in one go, and errors are returned as values instead of exceptions. A hello-world build is about 10.8 KB on Windows and runs even on DOS.
stories.heat: HN 127 pts / 96 comments (Show HN) · project page · velocity: low, posted 21 Nov
detail: The project page lists targets for Linux, macOS, Windows, WebAssembly and DOS on a 386, all checked by the same test suite. Reflection and async are not available. The core library is MIT-licensed and the bflat fork it builds on is AGPL-3.0.

stories.title: An experimental toolkit called gopgext lets developers write PostgreSQL extensions in plain Go, compiled with TinyGo.
stories.summary: Developers mark a Go function with a comment and the tool generates the C glue, install script and control file. The page warns it is not for production use.
stories.heat: HN 119 pts / 20 comments · project page · velocity: low, posted 21 Nov
detail: The Go code builds into a shared library that PostgreSQL loads, and PostgreSQL errors never unwind through Go frames. The project page warns that bugs run inside the database server and can crash it or corrupt data, and that the API may change without notice.

stories.title: Researcher Paulos Yibelo has published details of Upload2Shell, a Ghostscript bug that let crafted uploads run commands in apps such as WordPress, Roundcube and MediaWiki.
stories.summary: The use-after-free in Ghostscript's Type 1 font loader (CVE-2026-125396) escapes the -dSAFER sandbox. Ghostscript fixed it in version 10.08.0, and Debian and Ubuntu have shipped patched packages.
stories.heat: HN 77 pts / 30 comments · pwn.ai write-up · velocity: low, write-up updated 18 Nov, on HN 21 Nov
detail: The write-up lists affected downstream products including Debian 13 CUPS, Roundcube, Plesk, WordPress Core, MediaWiki PdfHandler, DokuWiki and ResourceSpace, some of them reachable without logging in. The bug was found on 27 July and the CVE published on 9 November.

sections.title: Geopolitics
sections.blurb: COP31 moves to approve a final climate text in Antalya, Mexico captures cartel boss El Chapo Isidro, the EU and UK seal three deals in Brussels, and Eisenkot opens coalition talks with Likud.

stories.title: COP31 presidents put a revised final text to nearly 200 countries in Antalya, with approval set for Sunday morning.
stories.summary: After talks ran past Friday's deadline and through Saturday, Turkey and Australia presented a new package early on 22 November. Summit president Murat Kurum says it addresses concerns on fossil fuels and adaptation finance.
stories.heat: Ground News 32 sources on the drafts (Left 47% / Center 47%) · Reuters, RTE, Arab News, Al-Monitor, GMA, The Print · velocity: high, decision due 22 Nov
detail: New since yesterday: the third draft has turned into a full package. Reuters, carried by RTE and Arab News, reports that Australia, which leads the negotiations, and Turkey, the host, announced the refined text after consultations with nearly 200 delegations. Delegations had until 03:00 GMT on 22 November to object, and a plenary session to start approving the deal was set for 06:00 GMT.

Kurum said: "We believe that we have put forward a text which all the parties can agree upon." He said concerns about fossil fuels, and about helping developing countries pay for adaptation, had been addressed. Reuters gives no wording from the new text on fossil fuels and no finance figures.

The earlier draft was criticised as lacking ambition because it did not mention an end to fossil fuel use. Activists held a silent protest outside the plenary hall, RTE reports. On 21 November the EU climate chief said the result would be "a good deal or no deal", and the United States is absent from the talks, according to Reuters via US News.

Ground News lists 32 sources on the draft texts, which accept that the world will pass the 1.5C Paris limit and call for removing 320 billion tonnes of CO2 this century with methods such as direct air capture. Hurriyet Daily News reports that delegates had already adopted some decisions, including on carbon market cooperation under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement.
This is the first COP since the UN confirmed that global warming is set to pass 1.5C. When this edition was compiled, no report confirmed that the text had been adopted.

stories.title: Mexico captured cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as El Chapo Isidro, and at least 11 people died in the violence that followed in Sinaloa.
stories.summary: Soldiers arrested him in Guasave, Sinaloa, on 20 November. He was on the FBI's Ten Most Wanted list, and gunmen blocked roads and burned vehicles after the arrest.
stories.heat: AP (via US News, Local10, WKBN), CBC, NBC News, Newsweek, Global Nation · velocity: high, 20-21 Nov
stories.about: Meza Flores is described by Mexican officials as a leader of the Beltran Leyva organisation and an ally of the Los Mayos faction of the Sinaloa Cartel.
detail: Mexico's Defence Ministry said he was arrested on Friday 20 November in Guasave, after more than a decade on the run. The FBI had offered a $5 million reward for him, AP reports.

The Defence Ministry said seven suspected cartel gunmen and four soldiers were killed in the violence after the capture. Security Secretary Omar Garcia Harfuch said troops would stay deployed in Sinaloa and called the arrest "an important step in pacifying Sinaloa". The DEA said it was a significant blow to the organisation. Experts quoted by AP warn that it could set off a new wave of fighting between cartel factions.

stories.title: The EU and UK agreed deals on food trade, emissions trading and a youth scheme at a Brussels summit with Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
stories.summary: The youth scheme would let 100,000 people under 30 from each side live, work or study in the other for up to three years. EU countries say they will hold off implementation until the UK agrees on university fees.
stories.heat: France 24 (AFP), Xinhua, Macau Business, Anadolu, Personnel Today · velocity: moderate, summit 20 Nov, reaction 21 Nov
detail: France 24 reports that Burnham met Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and Council President Antonio Costa on 20 November. The three agreements cut red tape for British food exports to the EU, link the UK and EU emissions-trading schemes, and create the youth experience scheme. France 24 says the deals will add $22 billion to the British economy. Anadolu adds that the two sides agreed to deepen cooperation on security, defence and migration.

Burnham called it a "landmark" deal and said talks on tuition fees will continue for six months. In a statement seen by AFP, EU countries said they would delay implementation until there is a fee agreement. Xinhua notes that all three deals still need formal approval, with the aim of applying them by 2028. Nigel Farage of Reform UK and the Conservatives criticised the deal as a betrayal of Brexit.

stories.title: Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party invited Netanyahu's Likud to a series of coalition talks starting on 22 November.
stories.summary: Yashar wants the broadest possible government with Eisenkot as prime minister. Likud answered with conditions, including that Netanyahu stays the sole prime minister and that Otzma Yehudit joins.
stories.heat: France 24 (AFP), ABC News Australia, Times of Israel, Jerusalem Post, TRT World · velocity: moderate, invitation 21 Nov, first meeting 22 Nov
detail: New since yesterday: Yashar announced on 21 November a "marathon" series of talks with Likud, with the first meeting on Sunday 22 November, France 24 and ABC News report. The Times of Israel reports that Likud demanded that Eisenkot's bloc stop its legislative agenda and its cooperation with Arab parties, that Netanyahu be the only prime minister, and that the far-right Otzma Yehudit party join the coalition.

Eisenkot has ruled out a rotation with Netanyahu and says he would lead any unity government that includes Likud. He repeats that he will form an emergency minority government if the broad coalition fails. The Jerusalem Post reports that negotiators from the two parties first met on 15 November, and that the vote for Knesset speaker is expected to be a point of dispute. No outcome of Sunday's meeting was reported when this edition was compiled.

stories.title: UN talks in Geneva on autonomous weapons ended without binding rules and only agreed to keep working until 2028.
stories.summary: The review conference of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons agreed to 'elaborate' a possible instrument by 2028. It set no date for treaty negotiations.
stories.heat: NPR, SWI swissinfo, Gizmodo, Business Upturn, Global Nation · velocity: moderate, ended 21 Nov
detail: The conference ran from 16 to 20 November and ended early on Saturday 21 November, swissinfo and NPR report. Because the CCW decides by consensus, states could not agree to start negotiations on a legally binding treaty, and the agreed wording leaves open whether any future instrument would be binding.
NPR says Russia did most to block a stronger mandate, while other reports also name the United States and Israel. The campaign group Stop Killer Robots called the mandate "watered down".

stories.title: Qatar pledged an extra 15 billion euros of investment in Germany during the emir's state visit to Berlin.
stories.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the money will go to areas such as artificial intelligence, semiconductors and aviation over five years. The two countries also signed two security and defence agreements.
stories.heat: Anadolu, Doha News, bluewin (dpa), LBC, Der Spiegel (via ua.news) · velocity: low, 20 Nov
detail: Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani met Merz in Berlin on 20 November at the start of a two-day state visit. Merz called for a "360-degree partnership" and said Germany is open to new partnerships in the defence industry, Anadolu and Doha News report. The two sides also agreed to work together against cyberattacks. Merz praised Qatar's role as a mediator between the US and Iran.

stories.title: A magnitude 6.7 earthquake struck Peru's Junin region with no casualties or major damage reported.
stories.summary: The quake hit near Ondores at a depth of about 82 miles, and there was no tsunami threat.
stories.heat: Anadolu only · velocity: low, 20-21 Nov
detail: Anadolu's 21 November briefing reports the quake near Ondores in central Peru. No other outlet was checked for this card.

sections.title: Krieg
sections.blurb: NATO chief Rutte says the alliance will defend every inch of Poland after the missile crash, two more tankers are hit off Oman as Iran keeps Hormuz shut, and Iran strikes a civilian plant in Bahrain while the Houthis fire missiles at Riyadh.

stories.title: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said in Warsaw that NATO will defend every inch of Polish territory, and NATO's North Atlantic Council meets on Monday about the Russian missiles that fell in Poland.
stories.summary: Rutte visited Warsaw on 21 November, a day after two Russian missiles and a drone came down in eastern Poland. Trump called the missiles a mistake, and Poland has not invoked NATO's Article 4.
stories.heat: Al Jazeera, France 24, Euronews, PBS, Kyiv Independent, Notes from Poland · velocity: high, new steps 21 Nov, council meeting due 23 Nov
detail: Speaking to reporters in Warsaw on Saturday 21 November, Rutte said "NATO will defend every inch of Polish territory", called the airspace violation "dangerous" and said allies stood "in full solidarity with Poland", France 24 reported. He said NATO worked "as it should" when allied jets supported Polish F-16s on Friday morning.

Polish Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said NATO's North Atlantic Council would meet on Monday in Brussels about the incident, according to France 24. Al Jazeera reported that Warsaw has stopped short of invoking Article 4, which provides only for consultations, and is seeking more support under NATO's Eastern Sentry mission, possibly including an airborne early warning aircraft.

Poland's defence minister said two missiles and a jet-powered drone fell at Nowy Lipowiec, Rudnik nad Sanem and Molodycz during Russia's overnight attack on Ukraine into 20 November; one missile was identified as a Kh-101 cruise missile. No injuries or damage were reported. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it "an intentional provocation".

Reactions split: US President Donald Trump played down the incident and called the missiles a mistake, while UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham called it "utterly unacceptable" and Germany's Foreign Ministry called it another Russian provocation, Al Jazeera reported. Al Jazeera found no Kremlin statement on the crash.

stories.title: Two tankers were hit by unidentified projectiles near Khasab in Oman on 21 November, and Iran's navy says a tanker caught fire after striking a mine east of the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.summary: The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre reported the two strikes with no casualties. Brent crude settled at $92.57 on Friday and still posted a third weekly loss.
stories.heat: Al Jazeera (AFP, Reuters), CBS News, ABC News, Jerusalem Post, straits.live · velocity: high, about three tanker incidents a day
detail: UKMTO said one tanker was hit at the rear about 20 km north of Khasab, on Oman's northern tip, and another was struck in its engine room about 31 km east of Khasab, Al Jazeera reported on 21 November. UKMTO did not say whether the reports involved separate vessels. No casualties were reported.

Iran's navy said on state television that an oil tanker caught fire after hitting a naval mine in a restricted area east of the strait, and that the ship had ignored warnings and sailed with its identification and navigation systems switched off. Al Jazeera could not verify it. The straits.live daily brief notes a separate Revolutionary Guards claim that two supertankers carrying more than 4 million barrels hit mines, and says no maritime authority has confirmed either claim.

Citing Iran's armed forces, Al Jazeera's Tehran correspondent said about 25 tanker incidents had been reported in the week since the previous Saturday. ABC News reported that attacks in and around the strait in October and November are the highest since the war began in late February. Iran says ships must coordinate with it and use lanes it sets; the US has answered by blockading Iranian ports and escorting tankers.

Brent settled at $92.57 a barrel on Friday 20 November, up 59 cents on the day after a tanker fire near the strait, but down about 3.4% on the week, its third weekly fall in a row, FinanceFeeds and IBTimes reported. Reuters, as quoted in those reports, said crude shipments through the strait have returned to roughly pre-war levels.

stories.title: Trump says he wants a permanent deal with Iran and is not rushing a decision on new strikes, after the Senate rejected a bill to limit his war powers by 48 votes to 51.
stories.summary: In a Fox News interview on 21 November, Trump said he wants an Iran deal that outlasts future presidents. CBS News sources say the US and Israel are considering a new attack on Iran in the short term.
stories.heat: CBS News live page, Dawn live page · velocity: medium, new remarks 20 and 21 Nov
detail: New since the last edition: on 21 November Trump told Fox News by phone that he wants a deal that lasts beyond future presidencies, saying "I'm not going to let somebody allow them to have a nuclear weapon", and that Iran breaks deals "the next day", CBS News reported. A day earlier he told Israel's Channel 12 he is "not rushing" and that "we'll see what happens after the new year starts."

On 19 November the Senate rejected a House-passed resolution that would have directed the president to remove US forces from hostilities with Iran, 48 to 51. Republicans Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and Rand Paul voted for it with every Democrat except John Fetterman, CBS News reported.

Iran's foreign ministry on 19 November rejected Trump's claim that Iran may be pursuing chemical or biological weapons, calling it part of the "same fraudulent script". CBS News also reported, citing sources, that the US and Israel are considering a new attack on Iran in the short term.

stories.title: Bahrain says an Iranian attack hit a civilian industrial facility and started a fire, while Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim they struck US bases in the kingdom.
stories.summary: Bahrain's Interior Ministry reported no injuries from the 21 November attack, the fourth attempted Iranian attack on Bahrain in about a week. The Guards' claims about US targets are not confirmed.
stories.heat: Al Jazeera, Arab News, Haaretz, US News (Reuters), CBS News · velocity: high, claims still coming on 22 Nov
detail: Bahrain's Interior Ministry said on 21 November that an Iranian attack hit a civilian industrial facility and caused a fire but no injuries; it did not name the site. Residents reported smoke over Sitra Island, home to a Bapco refinery, but that location is not confirmed, Arab News and Haaretz reported. Bahrain's Defence Force said air defences intercepted several attacks and that shrapnel caused minor damage.

The Revolutionary Guards said they fired missiles and drones at US positions at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases, and reports on 22 November said they also claimed hits on two US Patriot radar systems. Iran's IRNA said a US interceptor crashed on Sitra and started the fire. A US official told CBS News there were no impacts on US forces. CBS counted this as the fourth attempted Iranian attack on Bahrain in about a week.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia says it shot down three Houthi ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh on 21 November, as the Houthis hit back for the coalition's strikes on Hodeidah port.
stories.summary: It was the third night in a row of missile alerts in the Saudi capital. Yemeni government forces said they struck Houthi equipment in Marib the same day.
stories.heat: Al Jazeera, Arab News, Express Tribune, Manila Times, CBS News · velocity: high, third straight day of alerts
detail: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted three ballistic missiles fired toward Riyadh early on Saturday 21 November and later destroyed a Houthi drone aimed at the kingdom's south, Al Jazeera reported. Saudi civil defence had issued eight emergency alerts in the 24 hours from 7:30am on 20 November. A Houthi strike on 19 November damaged the Public Investment Fund tower in Riyadh.

Houthi media said the attacks were retaliation for the coalition's 20 November strikes on Hodeidah port, and the group again threatened Jeddah, other Red Sea ports and the Al-Shuqaiq power station. Yemeni government forces said they carried out six air strikes in Marib and fought in al-Jawf and Lahj. The Houthis claimed coalition strikes killed 41 people in 24 hours; government-aligned forces claimed 193 Houthi fighters killed or wounded. Neither figure is independently confirmed. Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar condemned the attack on Riyadh's financial district.

stories.title: A cargo ship bound for Russia's Kaliningrad caught fire after two drones hit it in the Gulf of Finland, and Finland brought back air and sea restrictions in the area.
stories.summary: The ship lost steering and drifted into Finnish waters on 21 November; its crew was evacuated. No one has said who launched the drones.
stories.heat: NBC News (Reuters), Yahoo News, UNITED24, France 24 · velocity: medium, new 21 Nov
detail: Leningrad region governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said two drones struck the vessel as it sailed toward Kaliningrad. Finland's Defence Forces said it was hit in international waters west of Russia's Gogland island, caught fire and drifted into Finnish territorial waters; the Finnish Border Guard said the crew left by lifeboat, and the Russian rescue ship Murman joined the firefight at Finland's request, Reuters reported via NBC News.

Finland's defence ministry reintroduced temporary aviation and maritime restrictions in the eastern Gulf of Finland as a precaution. Neither Finland nor Russia has named the attacker. UNITED24 noted that Ukrainian drones struck the Russian corvette Naro-Fominsk in the same gulf on 11 November, with no link established between the two incidents.

stories.title: The number wounded in Russia's strike on Kryvyi Rih rose to 60, and Zelensky said Ukraine still very much wants to join NATO.
stories.summary: Regional officials gave the new count on 21 November for the strike that killed a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old paramedic. A Russian drone also hit an apartment block in Kharkiv region, wounding 11.
stories.heat: France 24, CNN, Al Jazeera, Kyiv Independent · velocity: medium, follow-up to 20 Nov attack
detail: New since the last edition: Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha put the wounded at 60, including six children, up from the 42 reported earlier, France 24 reported. City head Oleksandr Vilkul said the strike damaged about 25 apartment buildings, a hospital and schools. CNN called it a "triple-tap" attack that also hit rescuers.

On 21 November a Russian drone hit a five-storey building in Kharkiv region, wounding 11 people including two children, and Russian officials said Ukrainian drones wounded three in Bryansk and Belgorod, France 24 reported. Zelensky told reporters "Of course Ukraine very much wants to be in NATO", after US envoy Jared Kushner said in Berlin that Washington could offer a guarantee similar to NATO's Article 5. Zelensky called Ukraine's strikes on the Kerch Bridge a "fair response".

stories.title: An Israeli strike on a food truck in Gaza City killed three people on 21 November, and Israel says it targeted Islamic Jihad militants.
stories.summary: Witnesses found meals in the truck with World Central Kitchen papers, but the charity says the truck was not its own. At least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire, by Palestinian count.
stories.heat: NBC News (Reuters), Times of Israel, Ground News article page · velocity: medium, 21 Nov
detail: Gaza's Health Ministry said three people were killed when Israeli forces struck the truck in Gaza City's Tel al-Hawa area. The Israeli military said it was targeting "Islamic Jihad militants in the area" and that the vehicle was carrying food to the group; Reuters could not verify this. Reuters video showed rice meals with World Central Kitchen papers, and WCK said the truck was not affiliated with it, though one driver had once worked for it, NBC News reported.

At least 1,600 Palestinians and five Israeli soldiers have been killed since the US-backed ceasefire of October 2025, according to Palestinian and Israeli tallies, and Israel now controls about two thirds of Gaza, NBC News reported. Gaza's civil defence said Israeli strikes killed six people in central Gaza the day before.

stories.title: Iran held two hours of talks with Qatari mediators in Tehran, and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the Strait of Hormuz will not be discussed until the US meets Iran's demands.
stories.summary: Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi described the Friday night meeting. Araghchi said reopening the strait is not difficult if Washington accepts what he called reasonable conditions.
stories.heat: Al Jazeera, CBS News, TASS, straits.live (12 outlets on the talks offer) · velocity: medium, 21 Nov
detail: Gharibabadi said a Qatari delegation met Iranian officials in Tehran for about two hours on the night of 20 November, Tasnim reported via Al Jazeera. Araghchi told state media the reopening of the strait is "irrelevant" until Iran's demands are met, called the visit routine mediation, and said there is "no solution" unless Washington admits its mistakes and keeps earlier commitments. On 15 November Gharibabadi had listed seven conditions for reopening, TASS reported.

stories.title: Israel says it struck a site in Lebanon's Bekaa Valley that Hezbollah was restoring for missile production, its second strike in the area in a week.
stories.summary: The strike near Janta was reported on 20 November with no casualties reported. Lebanon's state news agency said two Israeli drones also exploded on a building roof near Nabatieh.
stories.heat: Arab News, Asharq Al-Awsat, JNS, Xinhua · velocity: low, reported 20 Nov
detail: The Israeli military said its aircraft hit the entrances of a Hezbollah missile and weapons site near Janta after seeing members trying to restore it; Hezbollah did not comment, Arab News and Xinhua reported. Israel has kept striking Lebanon despite the truce, saying it is stopping Hezbollah from rebuilding, and the mandate of the UN force UNIFIL ends at the end of the year.

stories.title: A rights monitor accuses Sudan's Rapid Support Forces of killing three civilians in Abu Qalb, West Kordofan, accusing them of backing the army.
stories.summary: Sudan Tribune carried the report on 21-22 November as the army presses an air campaign against the RSF in Darfur and Kordofan. The RSF has not been quoted in response.
stories.heat: Sudan Tribune only · velocity: low
detail: Sudan Tribune reported the rights monitor's account that RSF gunmen shot civilians in Abu Qalb after accusing them of supporting the Sudanese army. The article could not be opened (blocked), so this card rests on the search summary of one report. Earlier, on 18 November, Darfur24 reported that the Kordofan Observatory counted at least 16 displaced people killed by an army drone strike on a school in Ghabish, West Kordofan.

sections.title: India
sections.blurb: Toxic liquor kills at least 11 in Manipur, Pant's century puts India far ahead in Wellington, Nepal's PM Balendra Shah arrives in Delhi, and the Nitish Setu opening turns into a naming row.

stories.title: At least 11 people have died and more than 180 are in hospital after drinking toxic liquor in Manipur.
stories.summary: Manipur's chief minister says 11 people died within 48 hours and has ordered an inquiry; officials suspect methanol in liquor linked to Sugnu town.
stories.heat: Ground News 43 sources (top India story, 44% Right) · Al Jazeera, US News (Reuters), Malay Mail, Business Recorder, Oneindia · velocity: high, reported 21 Nov, toll still being counted
detail: Al Jazeera and Reuters (via US News) reported on 21 November that at least 11 people died and more than 180 were hospitalised in Manipur after drinking illicit or adulterated alcohol. The state's chief minister gave the figure of 11 deaths in 48 hours.
The chief minister ordered an inquiry and said those responsible would be arrested. Officials suspect the liquor contained methanol.
Reports link the liquor to Sugnu town. People who had drunk alcohol from there in the past week were told to get a medical check.
Oneindia gives a higher count: 16 dead and more than 370 hospitalised between 15 and 20 November across Chandel and Kakching districts. The official figure and this count have not been reconciled.
Manipur is a dry state in name, but local and illicit liquor is widely sold. Methanol poisonings have killed dozens in other Indian states in recent years, for example in Tamil Nadu in 2024.

stories.title: Rishabh Pant scored 128 on day four of the Wellington Test, and India's lead over New Zealand grew past 300 runs.
stories.summary: India reached 675 for 6 against New Zealand's 368, and KL Rahul made 136. Pant became the first Indian wicketkeeper to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries.
stories.heat: AP (ABC News, Yahoo Sports), IANS, The Tribune, Sunday Guardian, Outlook, Stuff · velocity: high, play on 22 Nov (new since yesterday's 239/1 at lunch on day three)
detail: New since yesterday's edition: on day four at the Basin Reserve, Pant hit his ninth Test century, his first against New Zealand. He was out for 128 from 153 balls, with 12 fours and eight sixes, shortly before lunch.

IANS reported India at 629 for 6 at lunch, a lead of 261, with KL Rahul on 136. A later Sunday Guardian update had India at 675 for 6 after 161.3 overs, a lead of 307. No report seen had India declaring.

The Tribune says Pant is the first Indian wicketkeeper-batter with Test hundreds in Australia, England, South Africa and New Zealand. AP reports he moved past Brendon McCullum to second on the all-time list for Test sixes, behind Ben Stokes.
New Zealand made 368 in their first innings, built on a 216-run sixth-wicket stand between Henry Nicholls (175 not out) and Glenn Phillips (118), per Stuff.

stories.title: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah arrives in New Delhi today, and his talks with Modi on 23 November are expected to focus on flood reconstruction and air routes.
stories.summary: On his first official bilateral trip, Shah will meet President Droupadi Murmu and hold delegation-level talks with Modi, followed by a joint press conference.
stories.heat: Deccan Herald, The Wire, Amar Ujala (lead headline), IANS via Bhaskar Live, India News Network · velocity: rising, arrival 22 Nov, talks 23 Nov
detail: New since yesterday: reports now set out the schedule and the agenda. Nepal's foreign ministry says Shah travels at Modi's invitation for a two-day visit. IANS reports the delegation talks are on 23 November, followed by a joint press conference and a lunch hosted by Modi.

Flood reconstruction is expected to lead the agenda. Reports cite floods in Nepal that killed about 1,500 people and left more than 5,200 missing, with roads, bridges, power plants and homes destroyed.

The Wire reports that Kathmandu wants India to open more air routes through Indian airspace for flights into Nepal, a request successive Nepali governments have made without success. Trade, energy and infrastructure are also on the list.
Amar Ujala led its 22 November roundup with the visit.
stories.about: Balendra Shah, known as Balen, is a former mayor of Kathmandu and a structural engineer and rapper who became Nepal's prime minister after this year's election.

stories.title: Modi opened the Nitish Setu bridge in Bihar, and opposition leader Tejashwi Yadav said the bridge had already been in use since July 2025.
stories.summary: The six-lane Ganga bridge in Vaishali district was part of a Rs 34,000 crore package of projects; the opposition called the event self-aggrandisement and questioned naming it after Nitish Kumar while he is alive.
stories.heat: Deccan Herald (two reports), NewsBytes, Daily Jagran, Indian Masterminds · velocity: moderate, event 21 Nov, row continuing
detail: New since yesterday: the opening on 21 November turned into a political row. Deccan Herald reports that Tejashwi Yadav, Leader of the Opposition in the Bihar Assembly, said Nitish Kumar had already opened the bridge 17 months earlier and that vehicles had used it since July 2025.

Another report quotes Yadav saying the BJP was signalling Nitish Kumar's political end by naming a bridge after him while he is still alive. The BJP said the bridge was proof of development under Nitish Kumar.
Modi said Bihar is now known for development, not scams or crime, Deccan Herald reports. The projects opened in Vaishali are valued at about Rs 34,470 crore.
Reports differ on the bridge's length (9.76 km in one, 19.7 km in others).

stories.title: Uttar Pradesh police in Saharanpur gave AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi a guard of honour that was meant for a Supreme Court judge.
stories.summary: The police contingent at the Circuit House mistook Owaisi's convoy for the judge's, and a probe has been ordered.
stories.heat: Ground News 11 sources (55% Right) · Deccan Herald, IBTimes India · velocity: moderate, viral 21 Nov
detail: Deccan Herald reports that a police contingent was waiting at the Saharanpur Circuit House to salute a visiting Supreme Court judge on 21 November. When Owaisi arrived, the personnel took him for the judge and presented the guard of honour as he stepped out of his car.
Owaisi said he did not know the protocol and stood where he was told. IBTimes India reports that a probe was ordered.

stories.title: The Sensex gained 2.85% and the Nifty 2.61% in the week to 20 November, their fourth weekly rise in a row.
stories.summary: Both indices closed at nine-month highs, with banks leading; Business Standard credits foreign inflows, a stronger rupee and cheaper crude.
stories.heat: Business Standard, HDFC Sky · velocity: settled, markets shut for the weekend (new: weekly totals; daily close ran 21 Nov)
detail: New since yesterday: the weekly totals. The Sensex closed Friday at 83,919.71, up 2.85% for the week, and the Nifty 50 at 25,800.60, up 2.61%. It was the fourth straight weekly advance and both closed at nine-month highs.

The Nifty Bank index rose 2.49% for the week to 64,635.20 after an intraday high of 64,680.80. Business Standard links the rally to foreign portfolio inflows, a rupee rally and cooling crude prices; no weekly FPI figure was given.

stories.title: Adani Defence fired four of its Bagheera AT1 anti-tank guided missiles at the Pokhran range in front of Indian Army officials.
stories.summary: The company says the vehicle-mounted system has an 8 km range, about twice that of the Army's current land-based anti-tank missiles; the test does not mean an order has been placed.
stories.heat: Ground News 11 sources (73% Right) · ETV Bharat, Deccan Herald, The Defense News · velocity: moderate, test 20 Nov, reported 21 Nov
detail: Adani Defence and Aerospace says it demonstrated the Bagheera AT1 at Pokhran on 20 November under a 'No Cost No Commitment' trial watched by officials from the Army, the Department of Military Affairs and the Ministry of Defence. The system puts the missile, an automated launcher and day and night sights on a 4x4 armoured vehicle.

Performance figures come from the company: 8 km engagement range, up to 10 km for the wider missile family, and a two-missile salvo meant to beat a tank's active protection. One outlet notes that a demonstration is not a procurement decision; the Army still uses Milan-2T and Konkurs-M systems.

stories.title: Ladakh recorded a 70.03% turnout in its first panchayat elections as a Union Territory and 52.4% in its municipal polls.
stories.summary: Panchayat turnout was higher than the 67.8% of 2018, and polling teams were flown by helicopter to three remote stations in Zanskar.
stories.heat: PTI and IANS via Daily Excelsior, Free Press Journal, Greater Kashmir, India TV, ETV Bharat · velocity: moderate, polls 21 Nov, counting pending
detail: New since yesterday: the turnout. Reports put sarpanch turnout at 70.03% and panch turnout at 73.6%, against 67.8% in the 2018 panchayat polls. The municipal councils of Leh and Kargil drew 52.4%.

Polling covered 192 halqas across eight districts. Daily Excelsior reports that 55 sarpanches and 1,186 panches had already been elected unopposed, so voting was for the remaining 137 sarpanch and 242 panch seats. Sankoo had the highest sarpanch turnout at 75.20%. Lieutenant Governor VK Saxena praised the turnout, India TV reports. No results were out at the time of writing.

stories.title: Before the Tata Sons board meeting on 26 November, Noel Tata wants the board to take up an RBI-linked restructuring plan and a Rs 25,000 crore funding request from Shapoorji Pallonji.
stories.summary: The board, chaired by N Chandrasekaran, is expected to discuss listing Tata Sons, which Noel Tata and Tata Trusts oppose; one report says a trust may meet again before the board.
stories.heat: Business Standard, BusinessToday, Moneylife, The Open Press · velocity: building toward 26 Nov board meeting
detail: Business Standard and Moneylife report that Noel Tata, chairman of Tata Trusts, asked for two items on the 26 November agenda: a reorganisation plan to meet the RBI's rules without a stock market listing, and a proposed Rs 25,000 crore liquidity arrangement for the Shapoorji Pallonji Group against its 18.38% stake in Tata Sons.

New since yesterday's card on the Tata Trusts meeting: The Open Press reports that the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust may meet again before the board meeting, over concerns that the Tata Sons agenda was not shared with the trust and over consent under Article 121A. This rests on one secondary source.

stories.title: Delhi's air stayed in the 'poor' range on 21 November, and forecasters expect it to turn 'very poor' on Sunday, with fog likely for two days.
stories.summary: GRAP Stage I and II curbs remain in force after Stage III was lifted on 17 November.
stories.heat: The Statesman, IITM early warning system, Dynamite News, Amar Ujala · velocity: steady, seasonal
detail: The IITM early warning system put Delhi's AQI at 278 ('poor') at 09:00 IST on 21 November and forecast 'very poor' air for Sunday because of weak wind. The Statesman cites readings between 279 and 327 that morning and says Stage III curbs ended on 17 November while Stage I and II stay. Amar Ujala warns of fog across Delhi-NCR for the next two days.

sources.name: IITM Air Quality Early Warning System

stories.title: The Karnataka government asked the state police chief to act on blackmail and extortion complaints against the Power TV news channel.
stories.summary: A JD(S) legislator alleges the channel lured ministers and legislators with offers, recorded them in secret and broadcast the footage as stings.
stories.heat: PTI via ThePrint, Deccan Herald, UNI · velocity: moderate, letter dated 20 Nov, reported 21 Nov
detail: ThePrint (PTI) reports that the Home Department wrote to the DG-IGP on 20 November asking him to examine allegations of blackmail, extortion and entrapment against Power TV chief Rakesh Shetty and staff, act under the rules and report back. The complaint came on 3 November from C B Suresh Babu, JD(S) legislature party leader. The letter has gone to the Bengaluru police commissioner; Power TV had not responded.
On 28 October the Karnataka High Court had barred the channel from airing an alleged covert recording of former Magadi MLA A Manjunath, LiveLaw reports.

stories.title: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra told banks to lend more to small and micro businesses, saying such loans do far more for the economy than one large corporate loan.
stories.summary: Speaking at a financial inclusion camp near Pune on 21 November, he also warned people against get-rich-quick schemes.
stories.heat: Business Standard, Free Press Journal, NewsBytes · velocity: low, one speech on 21 Nov
detail: Business Standard reports that Malhotra opened a financial inclusion camp in Pune district focused on re-KYC. He said Rs 1,000 crore spread across small firms has far greater impact than the same sum lent to one big borrower; reports differ on whether he put the multiplier at 100 or 1,000 times. He said more than 60 crore bank accounts have been opened and the focus must move to financial and digital literacy. Similar camps run nationwide until 31 December.

sections.title: Cinema
sections.blurb: Sunrise on the Reaping heads for about $120 million, Ramayana Part 1 passes Rs 900 crore net in India, O.M: Operation Mole holds on day 2, a Home Alone sequel with Macaulay Culkin is in early works, and a film workers' body asks for protection for Saif Ali Khan and the Bachchans.

stories.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is now projected to open to more than $120 million in the US, Lionsgate's biggest opening since 2015.
stories.summary: Saturday estimates raised the prequel's three-day US opening from $110 million to more than $120 million, with about $200 million worldwide. Audiences gave it an A- CinemaScore, by most reports.
stories.heat: TheWrap, The Hollywood Reporter, Deadline (via Yahoo), ScreenRant, Variety · velocity: high, Saturday update 21 Nov, actuals due 22-23 Nov
detail: New since yesterday's edition: the weekend projection rose. TheWrap reported on 21 November that the film is heading for a $120 million-plus US opening from 4,018 cinemas, after a $56 million first day that includes $21 million from Thursday previews. Deadline had first put the Friday at about $51 million and the weekend at $110 million.

TheWrap says it would be Lionsgate's first opening above $100 million since The Hunger Games: Mockingjay Part 2 opened to $102 million in 2015, and that the film is taking an estimated 70% of all US box office this weekend. ScreenRant notes that a total above $121 million would beat Mockingjay Part 1 and give the franchise its third-best opening.
Deadline, as cited by Yahoo, projects about $200 million worldwide for the opening weekend, above its earlier forecast of $160 million to $190 million.
Most outlets report an A- CinemaScore, and several put the Rotten Tomatoes audience score at 95%. The Hollywood Reporter is reported as listing a B+.

Behind it, TheWrap's Saturday estimates put Amazon MGM's I Play Rocky at $9.3 million in its first wide weekend from 2,447 cinemas, Paramount's Ebenezer at $8.2 million in its second weekend (down 57%, $33 million total), and Warner Bros.' The Cat in the Hat at $7 million in its third weekend ($47 million total).

stories.title: Ramayana Part 1 crossed Rs 900 crore net in India on its third Saturday and reached about Rs 1,617 crore worldwide, by Sacnilk's count.
stories.summary: The film took Rs 27.40 crore net on day 17, up 74% from Friday, for an India net total of Rs 906.90 crore. Sacnilk says it is the third Indian film to reach Rs 900 crore net this fast, after Pushpa 2 and Dhurandhar 2.
stories.heat: Sacnilk, Koimoi, Bollywood Hungama, Flickonclick · velocity: high, third weekend jump on 21 Nov
detail: New since yesterday's edition (Rs 1,575 crore worldwide after 16 days): Sacnilk's day 17 page, last updated 21 November at 10:11 pm IST, gives Rs 27.40 crore net for Saturday 21 November, up 74.0% from Rs 15.75 crore on Friday. Hindi brought in Rs 20.25 crore of that, Malayalam Rs 2.75 crore, Tamil Rs 2.00 crore, Kannada Rs 1.65 crore and Telugu Rs 0.75 crore.

Sacnilk's totals after 17 days: Rs 906.90 crore net and Rs 1,083.70 crore gross in India, Rs 533 crore gross overseas, and Rs 1,616.70 crore gross worldwide. Koimoi puts the worldwide figure at Rs 1,612.54 crore.
Sacnilk says Ramayana is the third-fastest Indian film to Rs 900 crore net, after Pushpa 2 and Dhurandhar 2. Its worldwide total is now about Rs 125 crore short of Pushpa 2's Rs 1,742 crore.
Bollywood Hungama's own table showed Rs 25.32 crore for day 17 while the day was still being counted, and reported that the film has passed Rs 50 crore from 35 IMAX screens in 16 days.

stories.title: Dhanush's O.M: Operation Mole took about Rs 15.40 crore net in India on its second day, by Sacnilk's count, for a two-day total of Rs 33.50 crore.
stories.summary: Sacnilk shows a 14.9% drop from the first day and Rs 60.90 crore worldwide after two days. Other trackers report a steeper fall, so the day 2 figure is still disputed.
stories.heat: Sacnilk, Koimoi, ETV Bharat, The Week, India TV · velocity: high, day 2 on 21 Nov
detail: New since yesterday's edition: Sacnilk has revised the opening day to Rs 18.10 crore net (from Rs 17.70 crore) and gives Rs 15.40 crore net for Saturday 21 November: Tamil Rs 11.40 crore, Telugu Rs 3.50 crore and Hindi Rs 0.50 crore. Its two-day totals are Rs 33.50 crore net and Rs 38.90 crore gross in India, Rs 22 crore gross overseas and Rs 60.90 crore gross worldwide.

Koimoi's early trends put day 2 at Rs 15.5 to 16 crore and say the Hindi version is weak. ETV Bharat reported a much lower Rs 10.76 crore for day 2, a 41% drop, and linked it to poor reviews of the script. The Week, citing Sacnilk at 5 pm, said more than half of the opening came from outside Tamil Nadu.

The spy thriller, co-starring Mammootty, opened on 20 November against Aakasamlo Oka Tara, the Telugu film starring Mammootty's son Dulquer Salmaan. India TV reports that Aakasamlo Oka Tara took about Rs 3 crore gross on its first day, far behind O.M.

stories.title: A new Home Alone sequel with Macaulay Culkin returning as Kevin McCallister is in early development at Disney's 20th Century Studios, Deadline reports.
stories.summary: Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg are writing and producing the film, which started from Culkin's own idea. Disney declined to comment.
stories.heat: Deadline, IndieWire, TheWrap, The Hollywood Reporter, Yahoo · velocity: high, reported 20-21 Nov
detail: Deadline reported that the sequel is in early works, with Rogen and Goldberg's company Point Grey behind it. Culkin last played Kevin in Home Alone 2: Lost in New York in 1992, and pitched a sequel idea on stage at a fan event in Long Beach, California, last year. He played the character again in a McDonald's advert released on 17 November.

Open points, per the reports: whether the plot follows the father-and-son idea Culkin described in public, whether Chris Columbus, who directed the first two films, will return, and when Rogen and Goldberg can start, since they first have a horror film to prepare at Universal.

stories.title: A film workers' association has asked Maharashtra's chief minister to protect Saif Ali Khan, Amitabh Bachchan and Abhishek Bachchan after a series of threats against film stars.
stories.summary: The All Indian Cine Workers Association wrote to Devendra Fadnavis on 20 November. Mumbai Police are checking whether a threatening voice message sent to Saif Ali Khan is real or made with AI.
stories.heat: Bollywood Hungama, Outlook, The Tribune, National Herald, Filmibeat · velocity: medium, letter 20 Nov
detail: In its letter dated 20 November, the All Indian Cine Workers Association asks for more security for the three actors and their families, police protection at shooting locations and strict action against gang networks. It cites the October shooting incident involving Tiger Shroff in Juhu and warns that film production in Mumbai could stop if the threats continue, Bollywood Hungama and Outlook report.

The Tribune reports that Saif Ali Khan received a voice message, around 19 November, sent in the name of Zeeshan Akhtar, an accused in the Baba Siddique murder case, saying he would meet the same fate as Siddique. Forensic teams are checking whether the audio is an AI fake. Amitabh Bachchan's Juhu home, Jalsa, was named in hoax bomb emails sent to Mumbai and Pune police on 12 November. No arrest in the Saif Ali Khan case was reported by 21 November.
stories.about: The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) is a Mumbai body that speaks for film and TV crew and junior artists.

stories.title: Salman Khan apologised to Shraddha Kapoor because his film Maatrubhumi and her film Eetha both open on 4 December.
stories.summary: Salman Khan said at an ABP News event that he did not know about the clash and feels "really, really bad" about it. He said he called Shraddha Kapoor, who told him there is room for both films.
stories.heat: Bollywood Hungama, ABP News event · velocity: medium, 21 Nov
detail: Bollywood Hungama reported on 21 November that Salman Khan also asked people to watch Eetha. Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace, directed by Apoorva Lakhia, stars Salman Khan and Chitrangada Singh. Eetha, directed by Laxman Utekar for Maddock Films, stars Shraddha Kapoor as the Lavani dancer Vithabai Bhau Mang Narayangaonkar, with Randeep Hooda and Mohammed Zeeshan Ayyub.

stories.title: Sterling K. Brown is in talks to star opposite Nicolas Cage in Paramount's new Longlegs film, Deadline and Variety report.
stories.summary: Osgood Perkins writes and directs the film, which is set in the world of the 2024 horror hit and is due on 14 January 2028. The deal is not yet closed.
stories.heat: Deadline, Variety, The Playlist, Dread Central · velocity: medium, reported 20 Nov
detail: Deadline first reported the talks on 20 November and Variety confirmed them. Cage returns as the killer. The film is described as a new story in the same world, not a direct sequel, and Maika Monroe, who starred in the first film, is not expected to return.
The first Longlegs was released by Neon in 2024 and took $127 million worldwide on a budget under $10 million, Variety reports. The new film moves to Paramount.

stories.title: The 57th International Film Festival of India opened in Goa on 20 November with Pawel Pawlikowski's Fatherland.
stories.summary: The festival runs until 28 November under the theme "Stories Without Borders", with films from 86 countries. Anthony Chen's We Are All Strangers is the closing film.
stories.heat: PIB, DD News, Daijiworld, Variety (via Digg), Bollywood Hungama · velocity: medium, opened 20 Nov
detail: Daijiworld reports that Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant and festival director Ashutosh Gowariker opened the festival, and that more than 150 international films from 86 countries are showing. Spain is the Country of Honour. Four films from Assam, Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram are in the Indian Panorama section.

Fatherland won Pawlikowski the Best Director award at Cannes 2026. Bollywood Hungama reports that actor Abhishek Banerjee has two films at the festival: Bharatbala's Banaras and Sudip Sharma's Pushpak Vimaan.

stories.title: E.J. Carroll, an actor in The Deuce, Boardwalk Empire and the Law & Order series, has died at 66.
stories.summary: His representative told Deadline that Carroll died suddenly on 19 November on his way to a voice-over job. No cause of death was given.
stories.heat: Variety, TheWrap, Deadline (via Yahoo), ScreenRant · velocity: medium, reported 20-21 Nov
detail: Carroll played the sex shop owner Fat Mooney in HBO's The Deuce and Sheriff Victor Sickles in two 2012 episodes of Boardwalk Empire. His first screen credit was a police officer in Law & Order in 1998, and he later appeared in Law & Order: SVU and Criminal Intent. He also did voice work in the video games Grand Theft Auto V and Need for Speed: Undercover, Variety and TheWrap report.

stories.title: Enrica Perez's On Top of the Cliff won the Grand Prix at the 30th Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival.
stories.summary: The film, set in a Catholic girls' boarding school in 1950s Lima, won the 20,000 euro top prize on 20 November, and its lead Bianca Bucelli won Best Actress.
stories.heat: Variety, The Hollywood Reporter, Eye For Film · velocity: low, awards 20 Nov
detail: The jury was chaired by the playwright and screenwriter Christopher Hampton. The film is a co-production from Mexico, Peru and Switzerland. Swiss director Fred Baillif won Best Director for A Job Well Done, and When She Hears the Bells won Best First Feature, Variety reports.
